data.narrative:
RoboTwin is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing startup founded by Mejdrechová, Dvořák, and Polák, having raised €2.3M via EIC funding. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Stage-Progression methodology is the applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised (€2.3M) as a proxy for seed valuation and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression to the next financing stage yields an implied valuation of €5.75M. This method reflects the standard capital step-up observed in frontier-tech seed transitions, though it relies on the assumption that prior raises approximate post-money seed valuation.

Peer-Median triangulation cannot be applied due to insufficient comparable data. The broader sector contains ten peers, but only one same-stage comparable exists, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Expanding to all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable heterogeneity across valuation tiers and stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €5M to €7M, with a median of €6M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-peer benchmarking, which limits validation of the stage-progression result, and dependence on prior raise size as a proxy for seed valuation—a metric that may not reflect recent market conditions in frontier robotics.
